verdict.instructions: In this Arabic Islamic lecture transcript, determine whether `matched_span_in_lecture` (surrounded by `context_before` and `context_after`) is an actual quotation/citation of `canonical_corpus_text` (`source_type`), or if it is merely ordinary speaker prose/explanation that happens to share words with the corpus text. When `verses_in_passage` is present, the span is that many consecutive verses the engine found back to back: judge them together. When `neighbor_findings` is present, it lists the engine's nearest other findings before and after this one (unverified: they can be false too), with the words between them.

criteria.CORRECT: The speaker is genuinely quoting, reciting, or invoking this Quranic Ayah, Prophetic Hadith, or Dhikr (verbatim or as a direct religious citation in context).
criteria.FALSE: False positive: the words are ordinary conversational speech, fiqh explanation, or narrator/person names that coincidentally overlap with corpus vocabulary without quoting the text.
criteria.NOT_SURE: Ambiguous or partial paraphrase/meaning-only allusion where it is borderline whether the speaker intended a direct quotation.

start_missing.instructions: Was the START of this quote cut off from the detected span? `unmatched_corpus_prefix_words` are the words of the corpus text just before the part that was matched; `immediate_transcript_before` is what the speaker said just before the span; `prefix_words_heard` counts how many of the last corpus words before the span appear there (allowing ASR spelling errors). Answer true only if the speaker actually said words of the quote right before `matched_span_in_lecture`.

criteria.false: The span starts where the speaker started quoting: no words of the quote are missing at the start.
criteria.true: Words of `unmatched_corpus_prefix_words` were said right before the span and are missing from its start.

end_missing.instructions: Was the END of this quote cut off from the detected span? `unmatched_corpus_suffix_words` are the words of the corpus text just after the part that was matched; `immediate_transcript_after` is what the speaker said just after the span; `suffix_words_heard` counts how many of the first corpus words after the span appear there (allowing ASR spelling errors). Answer true only if the speaker actually said words of the quote right after `matched_span_in_lecture`.

criteria.false: The span ends where the speaker stopped quoting: no words of the quote are missing at the end.
criteria.true: Words of `unmatched_corpus_suffix_words` were said right after the span and are missing from its end.
